headline: Growth accelerates, restructuring charge widens GAAP loss
summary_short: BILL's fiscal Q4 2026 revenue rose 13.8% y/y to $436.2M and core revenue rose 15.8% to $400.5M, but a $76.6M restructuring charge widened the GAAP net loss to $18.5M even as non-GAAP net income climbed 52.5% y/y to $94.0M ($0.84 diluted).
summary_long: Revenue grew 13.8% y/y to $436.2M and core revenue rose 15.8% to $400.5M, driven by 17% growth in transaction fees on higher payment volume ($98.2B, +14.1% y/y) and 11% growth in subscription fees. GAAP operating loss widened to $34.3M from $22.3M a year ago on a $76.6M restructuring charge this quarter (none a year ago); ex-restructuring, non-GAAP operating income still rose 80% y/y to $101.6M. Net loss was $18.5M ($0.19/share) versus a $12.8M profit last quarter, while non-GAAP net income rose 52.5% y/y to $94.0M ($0.84 diluted). BILL repurchased ~$300M of stock and initiated FY27 guidance of $1.81-1.86B revenue (9-12% growth). Cash was $1,031.1M; businesses served fell 2.9% q/q to 479,300.

drivers.explanation: Transaction fees rose 17% y/y on higher payment volume and subscription fees rose 11% y/y, per the release's financial highlights.

GAAP operating loss widened primarily on a $76.6M restructuring charge this quarter versus none a year ago, per the non-GAAP reconciliation table; ex-restructuring, non-GAAP operating income rose 80% y/y.
The same $76.6M restructuring charge drives the swing from Q1's $12.8M profit and widens the y/y loss; non-GAAP net income, which excludes restructuring, rose 52.5% y/y instead.

Decline is concentrated in the 'Embedded Solutions and Other' segment (249,500 at June 30, 2026 vs. 266,700 at March 31, 2026); BILL AP/AR and Spend & Expense customer counts both grew over the same period.

CEO Rene Lacerte cited 'strong demand for BILL's integrated platform, with increasing adoption of our AI capabilities'; CFO Rohini Jain said the company enters FY27 on 'a clear path to meaningful GAAP profitability.'
